messages.author: 6e8a4aa79e627f0e
messages.subject: Predicting and backtranformation with covariates
parts:
Hello everyone!

I´ve been having some trouble with predict for some time now, and I really need your help.
My occupancy models have numeric covariates, and a few categoric, but none of those came up in the final selected models, so for example I have: 

occu(formula = ~1 ~ DAPROT + DFAGUA + DCENPOB + FELINO, data = umf)

Occupancy (logit-scale):
                           Estimate     SE      z          P(>|z|)
(Intercept)        -25.1            27.1   -0.925     0.355
DAPROT          21.0             23.0    0.915     0.360
DFAGUA         -40.9             44.9   -0.911     0.362
DCENPOB       -24.5            30.1   -0.814     0.415
FELINO          17.3               22.4    0.769     0.442

Detection (logit-scale):
 Estimate      SE       z       P(>|z|)
    -1.31      0.463   -2.84    0.00455

AIC: 41.22389 
Number of sites: 36
ID of sites removed due to NA: 1 5 6 17 23 42 43
optim convergence code: 1
optim iterations: 108 
Bootstrap iterations: 0 


I haven been able to backtransform my results in order to make my predictions

I have tried like this:

backTransform(fm80,"det")

Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Detection estimate(s)

 Estimate     SE LinComb (Intercept)
    0.212 0.0773   -1.31           1

Transformation: logistic 

backTransform(fm80,"state")

Warning message:
>In .local(object, ...) :
>Model did not converge. Try providing starting values or increasing maxit control argment.


But I know I'm missing something because of the covariates, and I so get this error.

Can you please help me?

Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 5fb191f8527859e2
messages.subject: Aw: [unmarked] Predicting and backtranformation with covariates
parts:
Laura,
backTransform() works for the detection model because there are no covariates. If does not work if there are covariates as it is the case for the occupancy/state part of your model. For this part of the model, you have to use the predict(). There are some examples in the unmarked documentation.
The estimates and SE in your model are very large. Something may be wrong. It may help if you standardize your covariates if you haven’t done so yet.
Best wishes, Beni

messages.subject: Aw: Re: [unmarked] Predicting and backtranformation with covariates
parts:
Laura,
 
>object 'fm.occu1' not found
This error messages states that this model is not in your workspace. You have to fit it to the data before you can use the predict() function.
 
newdat has the variable 'daprot' but the variable is called 'DAPROT' in the unmarked data frame and probably in model fm80. It should work if you use DAPROT = ...
 
I think this should work:
newdat = data.frame(DAPROT = seq( min(siteCovs$DAPROT), max(siteCovs$DAPROT), length.out=100 )) #seq rather than c
 
 
Best,
Beni

messages.author: bd00314644d53a96
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Predicting and backtranformation with covariates
parts:
Hello Laura,
I'm really a newbie in R and occupancy modeling, but I think I understand the solution to your problem.
First  you can use the backTransform () to estimate the parameters with covariates but it is used in the following way

backTransform (linearComb (fm62, type = "state", coefficients = c (1,0)))

  1 is your intercept and every 0 is the average of the covariate, there must be as many 0 as the number of covariates in your model, that is, if there are 4 covariates, you have to have four 0 (unless you want to estimate the value when determined covariable is different from your average).

this link could be of help
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/unmarked.pdf

However the predict function has more applicability

If you try to predict your example model, when you create the newdata you have to add the rest of the covariates and the way to do it depends if they are categorical or continuous. You would try in this way since your covariates are continuous

Newdat1 <- data.frame (FELINE = 0, DCENPOB = 0, DFAGUA = 0, DAPROT = seq (min (DAPROT), max (DAPROT)))

predict (fm80, type = 'state', newdata = Newdat1, appendData = TRUE)

Hope this can help you.
